title: Edge Anchoring and Capacity Slices Controller: latency-led regional anchoring with graceful shed paths
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and implement an 'Edge Anchoring and Capacity Slices Controller' to make routing decisions across regions based on latency SLOs, per-region capacity slices, and graceful circuit-breaker-driven fallbacks. The controller should: 1) prefer anchored regions for a customer to minimize egress/latency, 2) use real-time capacity hints to avoid routing to overloaded pools, 3) apply latency bucketing to preserve P50/P95 SLOs, and 4) provide deterministic shedding paths (soft and hard) that degrade QoS predictably rather than causing opaque failures.
goals: (1) Reduce cross-region tail latency by 15% for anchored customers under normal traffic. (2) Reduce global 99th tail error-rate during regional saturation by 40% via graceful shedding and fallback. (3) Provide observability surfaces for per-key anchor adherence and capacity breach events.
non_goals: This ticket does not implement autoscaling policies or change physical placement of GPUs. It does not alter customer billing or quotas; those will be separate follow-ups.
design_summary: Controller accepts a routing request with customer metadata, SLO weight (latency vs cost), and optional geo-anchor preference. It evaluates: 1) anchor affinity score (sticky weight + recency + customer override), 2) capacity slice availability (tokens, queue-depth, admitted QPS), 3) latency score (recent P50/P95 from telemetry), and 4) policy constraints (regional exclusions, legal). The decision is a ranked list of candidate regions with assigned 'steering action': DIRECT (route), HEDGE (parallel send to two cheap/warm regions), DEGRADE (route to lower-cost quantized model), or SHED (reject or async queue). Circuit breakers are triggered when capacity slice falls below soft or hard thresholds; soft triggers enable degraded paths, hard triggers initiate shed and notify SLA monitor.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Integration tests that simulate region saturation show controller chooses DEGRADE or SHED before latency SLO breaches in >90% of trials. 2) End-to-end canary traffic demonstrates no increase in P50 and <5% increase in P95 for anchored tenants under baseline load. 3) Logs and metrics: 'anchor_adherence', 'capacity_slice_util', 'breaker_state' emitted at 1m granularity. 4) Feature flag gating and rollout plan exist in a console page and can be toggled per-customer.
implementation_steps: 1) Add capacity-slice API for runtime pools (proto + runtime endpoint). 2) Implement affinity scorer in router module with pluggable weights. 3) Implement policy interpreter for allowed degrade/hedge actions. 4) Circuit-breaker state machine with soft/hard thresholds and hysteresis. 5) Integrate telemetry hooks for latency quantiles and capacity reporting. 6) Add e2e tests and chaos scenarios. 7) Rollout behind feature flag to internal orgs, then incremental customer ramp.
risks_and_tradeoffs: - Aggressive geo pinning increases chance of local saturation; mitigated by capacity-slices and hedging. - Hedges increase global cost; weigh against SLO penalties. - Degraded model routing may affect output quality; must be paired with structured output fallbacks. - Deterministic shedding could surface more rejections to customers vs opaque retries; choose communication strategy carefully.
metrics_to_track: anchor_adherence_rate, regional_capacity_utilization, routing_action_distribution (DIRECT/HEDGE/DEGRADE/SHED), request_latency_p50/p95/p99 by region, error_rate_by_breaker_state, fallbacks_triggered_count
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + canary in staging (2 days). Phase 1: Internal orgs only behind feature flag (1 week). Phase 2: 5% of traffic for selected enterprise customers (2 weeks). Phase 3: Gradual global enable with automated rollback on SLO regressions (monitoring + runbook).
notes: Prototype scoring was run in a synthetic load test showing improved P95 under moderate skew. We plan to expose per-customer preference for cost-vs-latency as part of onboarding. Consider follow-up to tie to billing analytics.
